gaps.sentence: The crisis could ___ the economic situation (WORSE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: worsen means to make worse. A base verb follows 'could'.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She gave a brief ___ of her plans (DESCRIBE).
gaps.explanation: After 'a brief' a noun is needed: description (-tion).

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The treaty will strengthen economic ___ between the two countries (COOPERATE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is followed by a noun: cooperation (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: The medicine is available without a ___ (PRESCRIBE).

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'signs of'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: After 'signs of' a noun is needed: recovery (the -er of 'recover' becomes -ery).

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.
